sanskrit: tathā bruvāṇaṃ saumitriṃ pradīptam iva tejasā abravīl lakṣmaṇaṃ tārā tārādhipanibhānanā
english: As Saumitri spoke thus, blazing as it were with energy, Tārā — whose face resembled the lord of stars — addressed Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: naivaṃ lakṣmaṇa vaktavyo nāyaṃ paruṣam arhati harīṇām īśvaraḥ śrotuṃ tava vaktrād viśeṣataḥ
english: "Do not speak thus, Lakṣmaṇa; the lord of the monkeys does not deserve to hear harsh words, especially from your mouth.

sanskrit: naivākṛtajñaḥ sugrīvo na śaṭho nāpi dāruṇaḥ naivānṛtakatho vīra na jihmaś ca kapīśvaraḥ
english: Sugrīva is not ungrateful, nor is he deceitful or cruel; the lord of monkeys is not a speaker of falsehood, O hero, nor is he dishonest.

sanskrit: upakāraṃ kṛtaṃ vīro nāpy ayaṃ vismṛtaḥ kapiḥ rāmeṇa vīra sugrīvo yad anyair duṣkaraṃ raṇe
english: This brave monkey Sugrīva has not forgotten the service rendered by Rāma in battle — what others would find impossible to do.

sanskrit: rāmaprasādāt kīrtiṃ ca kapirājyaṃ ca śāśvatam prāptavān iha sugrīvo rumāṃ māṃ ca paraṃtapa
english: By Rāma's grace, Sugrīva has here obtained glory, the eternal kingship of the monkeys, Rumā, and myself, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: suduḥkhaṃ śāyitaḥ pūrvaṃ prāpyedaṃ sukham uttamam prāptakālaṃ na jānīte viśvāmitro yathā muniḥ
english: Having lain previously in great misery and then attaining this supreme pleasure, he does not perceive the passing of time — just as the sage Viśvāmitra did not.

sanskrit: ghṛtācyāṃ kila saṃsakto daśavarṣāṇi lakṣmaṇa aho 'manyata dharmātmā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
english: Absorbed in Ghṛtācī for ten years, O Lakṣmaṇa, the righteous great sage Viśvāmitra reckoned it as but a single day.

sanskrit: sa hi prāptaṃ na jānīte kālaṃ kālavidāṃ varaḥ viśvāmitro mahātejāḥ kiṃ punar yaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ
english: If even Viśvāmitra of great splendor, the foremost among knowers of time, did not perceive time thus passed, what then of an ordinary man?

sanskrit: dehadharmaṃ gatasyāsya pariśrāntasya lakṣmaṇa avitṛptasya kāmeṣu rāmaḥ kṣantum ihārhati
english: For this one who has succumbed to the ways of the body, who is weary, O Lakṣmaṇa, and who is not yet sated in sensual pleasures — Rāma should bear with him here.

sanskrit: na ca roṣavaśaṃ tāta gantum arhasi lakṣmaṇa niścayārtham avijñāya sahasā prākṛto yathā
english: You should not, dear one, fall under the sway of anger, O Lakṣmaṇa, or act rashly without ascertaining the truth, like a common man.

sanskrit: sattvayuktā hi puruṣās tvadvidhāḥ puruṣarṣabha avimṛśya na roṣasya sahasā yānti vaśyatām
english: Men of true virtue such as yourself, O bull among men, do not suddenly fall under the sway of anger without deliberation.

sanskrit: prasādaye tvāṃ dharmajña sugrīvārthe samāhitā mahān roṣasamutpannaḥ saṃrambhas tyajyatām ayam
english: O knower of righteousness, I earnestly beseech you on Sugrīva's behalf — this great agitation born of anger should be relinquished.

sanskrit: rumāṃ māṃ kapirājyaṃ ca dhanadhānyavasūni ca rāmapriyārthaṃ sugrīvas tyajed iti matir mama
english: It is my opinion that Sugrīva would give up Rumā, myself, the kingship of the monkeys, and all wealth, grain, and treasures for Rāma's sake.

sanskrit: samāneṣvyati sugrīvaḥ sītayā saha rāghavam śaśāṅkam iva rohiṣyā nihatvā rāvaṇaṃ raṇe
english: Sugrīva will reunite Rāghava with Sītā — like the moon reunited with Rohiṇī — after slaying Rāvaṇa in battle.

sanskrit: śatakoṭisahasrāṇi laṅkāyāṃ kila rakṣasām ayutāni ca ṣaṭtriṃśat sahasrāṇi śatāni ca
english: In Laṅkā there are, it is said, hundreds of thousands of crores of rākṣasas, and thirty-six ten-thousands plus thousands and hundreds more.

sanskrit: ahatvā tāṃś ca durdharṣān rākṣasān kāmarūpiṇaḥ na śakyo rāvaṇo hantuṃ yena sā maithilī hṛtā
english: Without slaying those invincible rākṣasas who change form at will, it is not possible to slay Rāvaṇa, by whom the Maithilī was abducted.

sanskrit: te na śakyā raṇe hantum asahāyena lakṣmaṇa rāvaṇaḥ krūrakarmā ca sugrīveṇa viśeṣataḥ
english: They cannot be slain in battle without allies, O Lakṣmaṇa, and especially not Rāvaṇa of cruel deeds by Sugrīva alone.

sanskrit: evam ākhyātavān vālī sa hy abhijño harīśvaraḥ āgamas tu na me vyaktaḥ śravāt tasya bravīmy aham
english: Thus spoke Vālin, who was knowledgeable in these matters, the lord of monkeys. My information is not from direct knowledge — I speak from what I heard from him.

sanskrit: tvatsahāyanimittaṃ vai preṣitā haripuṃgavāḥ ānetuṃ vānarān yuddhe subahūn hariyūthapān
english: Indeed for the purpose of your assistance, foremost monkeys have been dispatched to bring back very many monkey troops — the leaders of monkey battalions for battle.

sanskrit: tāṃś ca pratīkṣamāṇo 'yaṃ vikrāntān sumahābalān rāghavasyārthasiddhyarthaṃ na niryāti harīśvaraḥ
english: Awaiting those valiant and supremely powerful ones, the lord of monkeys does not depart — for the purpose of accomplishing Rāghava's goal.

sanskrit: kṛtā tu saṃsthā saumitre sugrīveṇa yathāpurā adya tair vānarair sarvair āgantavyaṃ mahābalaiḥ
english: Moreover, a time limit has been set by Sugrīva as before, O Saumitri — today all those mighty monkeys are to arrive.

sanskrit: ṛkṣakoṭisahasrāṇi golāṅgūlaśatāni ca adya tvām upayāsyanti jahi kopam ariṃdama koṭyo 'nekās tu kākutstha kapīnāṃ dīptatejasām
english: Thousands of crores of bears and hundreds of golāṅgūlas will approach you today — abandon your anger, O subduer of foes! Many crores of brilliantly glowing monkeys will come to you, O scion of the Ikṣvāku line.

sanskrit: tava hi mukham idaṃ nirīkṣya kopāt kṣatajanibhe nayane nirīkṣamāṇāḥ harivaravanitā na yānti śāntiṃ prathamabhayasya hi śaṅkitāḥ sma sarvāḥ
english: Beholding your face and gazing upon your eyes reddened with anger, O one born to wound foes, the wives of the foremost monkeys find no peace — indeed we are all alarmed by this initial dread."

sanskrit: ity uktas tārayā vākyaṃ praśritaṃ dharmasaṃhitam mṛdusvabhāvaḥ saumitriḥ pratijagrāha tad vacaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Tārā with words that were humble and imbued with righteousness, Saumitri — gentle by nature — accepted those words.

sanskrit: tasmin pratigṛhīte tu vākye harigaṇeśvaraḥ lakṣmaṇāt sumahat trāsaṃ vastraṃ klinnam ivātyajat
english: When that speech was accepted, the lord of the monkey host cast off his great fear of Lakṣmaṇa as one sheds a wet garment.

sanskrit: tataḥ kaṇṭhagataṃ mālyaṃ citraṃ bahuguṇaṃ mahat ciccheda vimadaś cāsīt sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ
english: Then Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, removed the variegated, many-stringed, great garland from his neck and, free from intoxication, came to his senses.

sanskrit: sa lakṣmaṇaṃ bhīmabalaṃ sarvavānarasattamaḥ abravīt praśritaṃ vākyaṃ sugrīvaḥ saṃpraharṣayan
english: Sugrīva, the best of all monkeys, addressed Lakṣmaṇa of fearsome might with humble words, gladdening him.

sanskrit: pranaṣṭā śrīś ca kīrtiś ca kapirājyaṃ ca śāśvatam rāmaprasādāt saumitre punaḥ prāptam idaṃ mayā
english: "Lost prosperity, glory, and the eternal kingship of the monkeys — all this has been regained by me through Rāma's grace, O Saumitri.

sanskrit: kaḥ śaktas tasya devasya khyātasya svena karmaṇā tādṛśaṃ vikramaṃ vīra pratikartum ariṃdama
english: Who is capable of repaying such valor to that godlike hero, renowned by his own deeds, O warrior, O subduer of enemies?

sanskrit: sītāṃ prāpsyati dharmātmā vadhiṣyati ca rāvaṇam sahāyamātreṇa mayā rāghavaḥ svena tejasā
english: The righteous Rāghava will recover Sītā and will slay Rāvaṇa by his own might — with me serving only as an ally.

sanskrit: sahāyakṛtyaṃ hi tasya yena sapta mahādrumāḥ śailaś ca vasudhā caiva bāṇenaikena dāritāḥ
english: What need has he of allies — he by whom seven great trees, a mountain, and the very earth were pierced with a single arrow?

sanskrit: dhanur visphāramāṇasya yasya śabdena lakṣmaṇa saśailā kampitā bhūmiḥ sahāyais tasya kiṃ nu vai
english: He at whose mere twanging of the bow the earth with its mountains trembled, O Lakṣmaṇa — what need does such a one truly have of allies?

sanskrit: anuyātrāṃ narendrasya kariṣye 'haṃ nararṣabha gacchato rāvaṇaṃ hantuṃ vairiṇaṃ sapuraḥsaram
english: I shall accompany the lord of men, O bull among men, as he goes to slay the enemy Rāvaṇa along with his entourage.

sanskrit: yadi kiṃ cid atikrāntaṃ viśvāsāt praṇayena vā preṣyasya kṣamitavyaṃ me na kaś cin nāparādhyati
english: If I have transgressed at all out of trust or affection — as a servant — that should be forgiven me; there is no one who does not err.

sanskrit: iti tasya bruvāṇasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ abhaval lakṣmaṇaḥ prītaḥ preṃṇā cedam uvāca ha
english: As the great-souled Sugrīva spoke thus, Lakṣmaṇa became pleased and spoke to him with affection.

sanskrit: sarvathā hi mama bhrātā sanātho vānareśvara tvayā nāthena sugrīva praśritena viśeṣataḥ
english: "In every way my brother has a protector, O lord of monkeys — especially with you, O Sugrīva, as his modest and devoted guardian.

sanskrit: yas te prabhāvaḥ sugrīva yac ca te śaucam uttamam arhas taṃ kapirājyasya śriyaṃ bhoktum anuttamām
english: Such is your power, O Sugrīva, and such is your supreme purity — you deserve to enjoy the unsurpassed glory of the kingship of the monkeys.

sanskrit: sahāyena ca sugrīva tvayā rāmaḥ pratāpavān vadhiṣyati raṇe śatrūn acirān nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: With you as his ally, O Sugrīva, the mighty Rāma will slay his enemies in battle before long — there is no doubt in this.

sanskrit: dharmajñasya kṛtajñasya saṃgrāmeṣv anivartinaḥ upapannaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca sugrīva tava bhāṣitam
english: The words you have spoken, O Sugrīva, are fitting and proper, coming from one who knows righteousness, is grateful, and never turns back in battle.

sanskrit: doṣajñaḥ sati sāmarthye ko 'nyo bhāṣitum arhati varjayitvā mama jyeṣṭhaṃ tvāṃ ca vānarasattama
english: Who else, being capable and knowing what is fitting, deserves to speak thus — save my elder brother and yourself, O best of monkeys?

sanskrit: sadṛśaś cāsi rāmasya vikrameṇa balena ca sahāyo daivatair dattaś cirāya haripuṃgava
english: You are a match for Rāma in valor and strength — you have been given by the gods as his ally for a long time, O foremost of monkeys.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu śīghram ito vīra niṣkrāma tvaṃ mayā saha sāntvayasva vayasyaṃ ca bhāryāharaṇaduḥkhitam
english: But now, O hero, depart quickly from here with me and console your friend who is afflicted with grief over the abduction of his wife.

sanskrit: yac ca śokābhibhūtasya śrutvā rāmasya bhāṣitam mayā tvaṃ paruṣāṇy uktas tac ca tvaṃ kṣantum arhasi
english: And the harsh words with which I addressed you, having heard Rāma's words spoken in his grief-stricken state — that too you should forgive."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu sugrīvo lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā hanumantaṃ sthitaṃ pārśve sacivaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva spoke these words to Hanūmān, his minister, who stood at his side.

sanskrit: mahendrahimavadvindhyakailāsaśikhareṣu ca mandare pāṇḍuśikhare pañcaśaileṣu ye sthitāḥ
english: "Those who dwell on the peaks of Mahendra, Himavat, Vindhya, and Kailāsa, on Mandara, on Pāṇḍuśikhara, and on the five mountains —

sanskrit: taruṇādityavarṇeṣu bhrājamāneṣu sarvaśaḥ parvateṣu samudrānte paścimasyāṃ tu ye diśi
english: Those dwelling on mountains glowing with the color of the rising sun, shining in all directions, along the ocean's edge in the western direction —

sanskrit: ādityabhavane caiva girau saṃdhyābhrasaṃnibhe padmatālavanaṃ bhīmaṃ saṃśritā haripuṃgavāḥ
english: And the foremost monkeys who inhabit the fearsome forest of lotuses and palmyra palms on the mountain that is the abode of Āditya, resembling clouds at twilight —

sanskrit: añjanāmbudasaṃkāśāḥ kuñjarapratimaujasaḥ añjane parate caiva ye vasanti plavaṃgamāḥ
english: Those leaping monkeys who resemble the dark Añjanā cloud, who possess the strength of elephants, and who dwell on and beyond Mount Añjanā —

sanskrit: manaḥśilā guhāvāsā vānarāḥ kanakaprabhāḥ merupārśvagatāś caiva ye ca dhūmragiriṃ śritāḥ
english: Those monkeys of golden radiance who dwell in caves of red arsenic ore, those ranging the slopes of Meru, and those who have taken refuge on the smoky mountain —

sanskrit: taruṇādityavarṇāś ca parvate ye mahāruṇe pibanto madhumaireyaṃ bhīmavegāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: And those leaping monkeys of fearsome speed, colored like the young sun, who drink honey-wine on the great red mountain —

sanskrit: vaneṣu ca suramyeṣu sugandhiṣu mahatsu ca tāpasānāṃ ca ramyeṣu vanānteṣu samantataḥ
english: And those dwelling in very beautiful, fragrant, great forests, and in the pleasant forest margins of ascetics, on all sides —

sanskrit: tāṃs tāṃs tvam ānaya kṣipraṃ pṛthivyāṃ sarvavānarān sāmadānādibhiḥ kalpair āśu preṣaya vānarān
english: Bring all those various monkeys throughout the earth quickly; dispatch the monkeys swiftly by means of conciliation, gifts, and such other expedients.

sanskrit: preṣitāḥ prathamaṃ ye ca mayā dūtā mahājavāḥ tvaraṇārthaṃ tu bhūyas tvaṃ harīn saṃpreṣayāparān
english: Those swift messengers who were previously dispatched by me — for the purpose of hastening them, send yet more monkeys additionally.

sanskrit: ye prasaktāś ca kāmeṣu dīrghasūtrāś ca vānarāḥ ihānayasva tān sarvāñ śīghraṃ tu mama śāsanāt
english: Those monkeys who are absorbed in pleasures or who are dilatory — bring all of them here quickly by my command.

sanskrit: ahobhir daśabhir ye ca nāgacchanti mamājñayā hantavyās te durātmāno rājaśāsanadūṣakāḥ
english: Those wicked ones who do not come within ten days by my order — they are to be slain, for they are violators of the royal command.

sanskrit: śatāny atha sahasrāṇi koṭyaś ca mama śāsanāt prayāntu kapisiṃhānāṃ diśo mama mate sthitāḥ
english: Hundreds, thousands, and crores of lion-like monkeys, abiding by my will, are to set out in the various directions at my command.

sanskrit: meghaparvatasaṃkāśāś chādayanta ivāmbaram ghorarūpāḥ kapiśreṣṭhā yāntu macchāsanād itaḥ
english: Resembling clouds and mountains, seemingly covering the sky, the foremost monkeys of fearsome appearance are to depart from here at my command.

sanskrit: te gatijñā gatiṃ gatvā pṛthivyāṃ sarvavānarāḥ ānayantu harīn sarvāṃs tvaritāḥ śāsanān mama
english: Knowing the ways and having traversed all routes, all those monkeys throughout the earth are to bring all the monkeys here swiftly, in accordance with my command."

sanskrit: tasya vānararājasya śrutvā vāyusuto vacaḥ dikṣu sarvāsu vikrāntān preṣayām āsa vānarān
english: Hearing the words of the monkey king, the son of Vāyu dispatched valiant monkeys in all directions.

sanskrit: te padaṃ viṣṇuvikrāntaṃ patatrijyotiradhvagāḥ prayātāḥ prahitā rājñā harayas tatkṣaṇena vai
english: Traversing the path measured by Viṣṇu's stride, following the route of birds and lightning, those monkeys sent forth by the king departed instantly.

sanskrit: te samudreṣu giriṣu vaneṣu ca saritsu ca vānarā vānarān sarvān rāmahetor acodayan
english: Those monkeys spurred on all monkeys — in the oceans, on mountains, in forests, and along rivers — for the sake of Rāma.

sanskrit: mṛtyukālopamasyājñāṃ rājarājasya vānarāḥ sugrīvasyāyayuḥ śrutvā sugrīvabhayadarśinaḥ
english: Hearing the command of Sugrīva, king of kings, which was like the call of death, the monkeys came — having perceived the terror of Sugrīva's wrath.

sanskrit: tatas te 'ñjanasaṃkāśā gires tasmān mahājavāḥ tisraḥ koṭyaḥ plavaṃgānāṃ niryayur yatra rāghavaḥ
english: Then three crores of leaping monkeys, resembling collyrium, of great speed, issued forth from that mountain to where Rāghava was.

sanskrit: astaṃ gacchati yatrārkas tasmin girivare ratāḥ taptahemasamābhāsās tasmāt koṭyo daśacyutāḥ
english: From that excellent mountain where the sun sets, where they delight — those resembling refined gold in their brilliance — ten crores issued forth.

sanskrit: kailāsa śikharebhyaś ca siṃhakesaravarcasām tataḥ koṭisahasrāṇi vānarāṇām upāgaman
english: From the peaks of Kailāsa came thousands of crores of monkeys with the lustre of lion manes.

sanskrit: phalamūlena jīvanto himavantam upāśritāḥ teṣāṃ koṭisahasrāṇāṃ sahasraṃ samavartata
english: Those who live on fruits and roots and dwell on Himavat — from among them thousands of crores arrived, numbering a thousand.

sanskrit: aṅgāraka samānānāṃ bhīmānāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām vindhyād vānarakoṭīnāṃ sahasrāṇy apatan drutam
english: From the Vindhya, resembling burning coals, fearsome and of fearsome deeds — thousands of crores of monkeys rushed forth swiftly.

sanskrit: kṣīrodavelānilayās tamālavanavāsinaḥ nārikelāśanāś caiva teṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate
english: Those dwelling on the shores of the milk ocean, inhabiting forests of tamāla trees, and feeding on coconuts — their number is beyond reckoning.

sanskrit: vanebhyo gahvarebhyaś ca saridbhyaś ca mahājavāḥ āgacchad vānarī senā pibantīva divākaram
english: From forests, from caverns, and from rivers, the monkey army came at great speed — as if drinking up the sun.

sanskrit: ye tu tvarayituṃ yātā vānarāḥ sarvavānarān te vīrā himavac chailaṃ dadṛśus taṃ mahādrumam
english: Those valiant monkeys who had gone to hasten all the monkeys beheld the Himavat mountain with its great trees.

sanskrit: tasmin girivare ramye yajño maheśvaraḥ purā sarvadevamanastoṣo babhau divyo manoharaḥ
english: On that excellent, beautiful mountain a great sacrifice had once been performed by Maheśvara — divine, enchanting, and pleasing to the minds of all gods — and its glory still shone.

sanskrit: annaviṣyandajātāni mūlāni ca phalāni ca amṛtasvādukalpāni dadṛśus tatra vānarāḥ
english: There the monkeys saw roots and fruits born from the flowing of the sacrificial food — tasting like nectar in flavor.

sanskrit: tad anna saṃbhavaṃ divyaṃ phalaṃ mūlaṃ manoharam yaḥ kaś cit sakṛd aśnāti māsaṃ bhavati tarpitaḥ
english: That divine, enchanting fruit and root born of the sacrificial food — whoever eats even once becomes satisfied for a full month.

sanskrit: tāni mūlāni divyāni phalāni ca phalāśanāḥ auṣadhāni ca divyāni jagṛhur hariyūthapāḥ
english: Those fruit-eating leaders of monkey troops gathered those divine roots, fruits, and divine herbs.

sanskrit: tasmāc ca yajñāyatanāt puṣpāṇi surabhīṇi ca āninyur vānarā gatvā sugrīvapriyakāraṇāt
english: Going there, the monkeys also brought back fragrant flowers from that sacrificial ground — for the sake of pleasing Sugrīva.

sanskrit: te tu sarve harivarāḥ pṛthivyāṃ sarvavānarān saṃcodayitvā tvaritaṃ yūthānāṃ jagmur agrataḥ
english: And all those foremost monkeys, having swiftly urged on all the monkeys throughout the earth, marched at the head of the troops.

sanskrit: te tu tena muhūrtena yūthapāḥ śīghrakāriṇaḥ kiṣkindhāṃ tvarayā prāptāḥ sugrīvo yatra vānaraḥ
english: In that very hour, those swift-acting troop leaders swiftly reached Kiṣkindhā, where Sugrīva the monkey dwelt.

sanskrit: te gṛhītvauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ phalaṃ mūlaṃ ca vānarāḥ taṃ pratigrāhayām āsur vacanaṃ cedam abruvan
english: Those monkeys, having taken all the herbs, fruits, and roots, presented them to him and spoke these words.

sanskrit: sarve parigatāḥ śailāḥ samudrāś ca vanāni ca pṛthivyāṃ vānarāḥ sarve śāsanād upayānti te
english: "All the mountains, oceans, and forests have been traversed; all the monkeys of the earth are coming at your command."

sanskrit: evaṃ śrutvā tato hṛṣṭaḥ sugrīvaḥ plavagādhipaḥ pratijagrāha ca prītas teṣāṃ sarvam upāyanam
english: Hearing this, Sugrīva, lord of the leaping monkeys, was overjoyed and gladly accepted all the gifts they had brought.
